title: Works in Which Copyright Subsists and Exclusive Rights of Authors
content:
Section 13 of the Copyright Act, 1957 provides that copyright subsists in original literary, dramatic, musical, and artistic works, cinematograph films, and sound recordings. Section 14 enumerates the exclusive rights of the owner, including reproduction, publication, adaptation, and translation.

Key Legal Implications for Traditional Medicine Knowledge & Compendia:
1. Ancient classical Sanskrit verses and foundational treatises (e.g., Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita, Ashtanga Hridaya) are in the public domain; their underlying ancient text cannot be monopolized by copyright.
2. Modern scholarly commentaries, original English/vernacular translations, explanatory annotations, structured clinical dossiers, botanical drawings, and proprietary compilations of Ayurvedic formulation databases are original literary/artistic works entitled to copyright protection.
3. Electronic database compilations (e.g., TKDL's curated classifications) enjoy protection as literary compilations under Section 2(o).
